previous_description: Defines reusable animation and transition patterns for state changes, page navigation, or component lifecycle events. Ensures consistent motion design across the application.
definition: A reusable motion definition specifying the animation type, duration and easing applied when a UI change occurs, such as a state change, route change, or component enter/leave. It describes how the change is animated, not which change occurs, and can be shared by many state transitions, patterns and views.

distinguish_from.when: the element is a concrete edge in an ExperienceState machine with a source state, destination state, trigger and guard, whether or not it is animated.
the reusable artifact describes the interaction itself (trigger modality, feedback such as toast or modal, target), rather than the motion curve and duration of the visual change.
the reusable definition is an operation executed during a transition (navigate, submit, dispatch, validate), not an animation.
the reusable artifact is a whole state machine of named states and transitions, such as a wizard or optimistic update.

standard_reference: CSS Transitions Module Level 1 (transition-duration, transition-timing-function); Web Animations API
code_evidence: Named, shared animation definitions such as Angular `trigger('fadeIn', [transition(':enter', [animate('300ms ease-in')])])` or exported Framer Motion `variants` objects imported by several components

CSS classes or @keyframes reused across components for enter/leave or route changes (e.g. `.fade-enter-active { transition: opacity 300ms ease-in-out }` used with Vue `<Transition name="fade">` or react-transition-group `CSSTransition classNames="slide"`)

Motion design tokens or theme entries defining duration and easing values (e.g. `motion.duration.medium: 300ms`, `motion.easing.standard: cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)`) referenced by page-transition or modal-open animations

attribute_descriptions.name: to
attribute_descriptions.description: The target end state of the animation: a specNodeId of the ExperienceState, View or SubView being entered, or a generic lifecycle target such as 'enter' or 'leave'. Set it to the narrowest target the template is meant for.

attribute_descriptions.name: trigger
attribute_descriptions.description: The event or change that starts the animation, e.g. 'route-change', 'state-change', 'mount', 'unmount', or a DOM event name such as 'click'. Set it so the template can be matched to the transitions it governs.

attribute_descriptions.name: description
attribute_descriptions.description: Free-text summary of the motion's intent and visual effect (e.g. 'modal slides up from bottom and fades in'). Set it whenever the name alone does not convey the effect.

notes: Required 'to' contradicts reusability, because a template bound to one destination duplicates StateTransition.to. Make 'to' optional, or redefine it as a lifecycle target. 'trigger' is free text while StateTransition.trigger is an enum, so align them. Consider adding delay, direction and iteration attributes. The name invites confusion with StateTransition; 'MotionTemplate' would be clearer.
